primary_source: Selling 1877, second part, Fig.1/Tafel III; source states six intersections of the six indicated symmetry axes are fourfold symmetry centres, with right-angle marks indicating the fourfold symmetry.
source_exact_constraints: exactly six indicated axis intersections are fourfold centres
right-angle marks encode the fourfold symmetry
dotted lines in Fig.1 denote symmetry axes
boundary letters denote the variable quantity vanishing on that boundary
the external-boundary transformation semantics P,Q,R,S must be attached before promotion of a historical curve/reflection
attempt: Direct inspection plus machine-readable vector tables was used to seek six individually addressable right-angle/fourfold-centre markers. No coordinate was promoted from visual impression alone.
reason_for_nonpromotion: The current vectorization exposes only two degree-4 solid diagnostic nodes, while the source requires six special centres and explicitly allows a curved/folded representation of the symmetry axes. The source text fixes count/type but does not provide a machine-readable unique mapping from six right-angle marks to present node IDs. A visual-only selection would violate the provenance gate.
guard: Absence of a unique current raster binding is not a non-existence statement about the six historical centres.
